summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Emerald Health through the Console usage analytics and per-route cost breakdown. Key focus: how per-route dashboards map to token cost, SLA reporting, and options for dedicated vs hosted. Customer requested pricing, security docs (SOC2/network), and a short pilot to benchmark latency/cost with their traffic.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48m
Attendees: Maya Ortiz (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Sandra Li (Emerald Head of AI), Ravi Malhotra (Platform), Priya Rao (Security)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Maya from Redwood, and with me is Ethan our solutions engineer. how's everybody doing?
[00:07] Sandra: good, thanks, we just wrapped another sprint so perfect timing.
[00:10] Ethan: great, i'll take us through the console, mostly focusing on usage analytics, per-route dashboards and the cost breakdown, and then we'll leave time for questions.
[00:18] Priya: quick note - i'll be asking a few security questions around logs and retention.
[00:22] Maya: perfect, we'll cover that. just to confirm context, Sandra, you mentioned you want to measure cost by route and have SLA alerts for your clinical QA flows?
[00:30] Sandra: yes, we have three main routes - triage summary, patient note generation, and similarity search for record matching. the triage one is latency-sensitive, the others are more batch-y.
[00:40] Ethan: cool, that matches what we see at similar customers. i'm going to share my screen now - opening Redwood Consle - excuse me, console - small typo but you know the drill.
[00:50] [screen share audio] Ethan: top-level: usage timeline by token, model mix, and route. here you can filter by date, team, and model version. the per-route dashboards break down average latency, p95, tokens in/out, and cost per 1k tokens.
[01:10] Sandra: how does the console attribute cost to a route if multiple models are used in a flow?
[01:15] Ethan: good q; we attribute at request-level using the model id attached to the request. if you have multi-step pipelines, you can either report per-step or aggregated per-route. the console shows both. small caveat - if you use fallback routing it may show multiple model rows, but totals are consistent. sometimes the transcription shows 'fallback routinng' - that's just the UI name.
[01:35] Ravi: and cost model - is it per-token billed exactly like the hosted API?
[01:40] Maya: yes, for hosted it's per-token and per-embedding units. for Dedicated we provide reserved capacity pricing which smooths cost but you still get per-token internal accounting in the console so you can see unit economics.
[01:52] Priya: on the security side, can we see audit logs for per-route requests and who invoked them? retention?
[01:58] Ethan: yes - audit logs are available and can be exported to your SIEM. retention is configurable with enterprise tiers; we have SOC2 docs that detail this. note that private deployments (VPC/on-prem) let you keep logs in your own bucket.
[02:12] Sandra: show me an example of the cost breakdown for patient note generation.
[02:15] Ethan: sure - switching to route 'patient-note-gen'. here you see tokens in, tokens out, model selection heatmap, and a cost column that splits infrastructure (GPU time) vs model license/usage. downstream we show per-token unit cost and running estimated monthly bill.
[02:32] [02:32] Ethan: sometimes the kernel names come through funny in our transcripts - 'compilation and kernel selection' is the runtime choosing the best kernels based on sequence length etc. that affects cost.
[02:42] Sandra: can we group by request metadata, e.g., priority=low/high?
[02:45] Ethan: yep, you can tag requests and then the dashboards can filter and group by that metadata. that's how you can isolate triage fast-path vs batch.
[02:55] Ravi: latency SLOs - can the console show SLO burn rates per route?
[02:59] Ethan: yes p95/p99 trends and SLO burn rate charts are built-in. you can set SLO thresholds per-route and get alerts to PagerDuty or Slack.
[03:10] Sandra: about KV cache and batching optimizations - will the console tell us how much KV cache hit rate saved us?
[03:17] Ethan: we show cache hit/miss metrics and estimate token savings from KV cache & batching. sometimes the transcriber turns KV cache into 'KV cash' in the raw export - ignore that lol.
[03:26] Priya: encryption at rest - KMS support?
[03:29] Maya: yes, customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated. Hosted supports KMS with Redwood-managed keys or can integrate with customer KMS depending on contract.
[03:37] Priya: and SSO / RBAC?
[03:40] Ethan: SAML SSO, role-based access controls scoped by team and route, and per-token audit trails.
[03:46] Sandra: what's the typical cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated for a high-throughput route?
[03:50] Maya: it depends on utilization - Dedicated generally gives you lower marginal token cost if you sustain high throughput because of reserved GPU hours. Hosted is simpler and good for spiky usage. we usually run a break-even calc - the console's cost estimator will show you the point at which Dedicated pays off given your traffic pattern.
[04:05] Sandra: can you show the estimator?
[04:07] Ethan: switching to Cost Explorer -> estimator. input your monthly token volume and model mix; it projects hosted vs dedicated spend and shows a suggested Dedicated pool size and expected p95 latency.
[04:20] Ravi: how accurate is that estimator? do you base it on live kernel perf numbers?
[04:24] Ethan: it's based on Redwood-verified performance profiles per model/version and your observed sequence length distribution; we also use running telemetry if you enable telemetry sharing for the pilot. accuracy is usually within 10-15% for similar workloads.
[04:38] Sandra: about private deployment - we have strict data residency rules. can we run the console control plane in our VPC?
[04:44] Maya: yes, Private offers a customer-managed control plane with VPC peering or full on-prem. we'll include network diagrams in the security packet.
[04:52] Priya: and do you support HSMs?
[04:55] Ethan: yes we can integrate HSM for key storage in Private deployments.
[05:00] [05:00] Sandra: curious - on anomalies, can the console detect quality regressions i.e., model output drift vs a baseline?
[05:07] Ethan: we have quality monitoring tied to evals and prompt sets. the console can surface regressions based on your test prompts and send alerts if output metrics shift.
[05:17] Sandra: great. what about model rollouts and automatic fallback policies?
[05:20] Ethan: rollouts are supported. you can do canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to a compatible variant if the new model breaches latency/cost/quality thresholds. the routing policy graph shows fallbacks.
[05:33] Ravi: for the pilot we're thinking of running triage route at 100 qps with 0.6 avg seq length, estimate cost?
[05:40] Maya: we'll run numbers after the call - Ethan will ask for sample traffic and we'll plug into the estimator and return a projection.
[05:47] Priya: any compliance artifacts you can share?
[05:50] Maya: yes SOC2, ISO if required, network diagrams, pen test reports - we'll include them in the follow up.
[05:56] [screen share pauses] Ethan: quick demo of alerts - here is a route-level alert that triggered when p95 rose above 600ms for 5 minutes. you can drill into the offending requests and see model versions, kernel decisions, and batching params.
[06:15] Sandra: can we export the per-route cost report as CSV on a schedule?
[06:18] Ethan: yes scheduled exports or API access. you can pull raw usage rows with request-level metadata.
[06:24] Sandra: curious about token accounting for embeddings versus text generation in a route that does both.
[06:29] Ethan: the console splits units: embedding units vs text tokens; you can see them separately and get a combined cost column.
[06:36] Maya: ok time check - about 30 minutes in, want to make sure we cover pricing and next steps.
[06:41] Sandra: yes please.
[06:43] Maya: summary: we'll send pricing for hosted and recommended dedicated config, security pack, and Ethan will run a benchmark script with your sample traffic. Ravi you'll share sample traffic. any other items?
[06:55] Ravi: i'll try to get the traffic by Tuesday.
[06:58] Priya: i'll review the SOC2 and network diagrams once you send them.
[07:02] Sandra: quick follow-up: can we add a view that shows cost per 1k successful clinical completions?
[07:08] Ethan: yes you can add custom derived metrics in the dashboard. we'll include a how-to doc.
[07:12] Maya: excellent. thanks everyone - we'll recap in an email and attach the artifacts.
[07:18] Sandra: thank you.

[END]

Notes: transcript contains typical speech artifacts, some mis-heard product names and slight stutters. The structure includes header, summary, topics and a natural transcript with timestamps.

Recap / Next steps (as discussed in call):
- Maya to send pricing and Dedicated sizing options, and security packet (SOC2, network diagram)
- Ethan to share benchmark script and run the pilot with Emerald sample traffic
- Ravi to provide sample traffic and API access for pilot
notes: Customer is leaning toward a short Dedicated pilot for triage route to validate latency and cost. Security and compliance questions are gating. AE recommends pilot before committing to Dedicated.
